text:
incident-bot: ALERT › p99 tail latency spike for customer 'Cerulean' (single-tenant pool c-cerulean-prod). p95 also elevated. Streaming stalls reported. Paging on-call.
Maya (oncall): acked, oncall here. getting dashboard now. can someone post the p95/p99 numbers and affected routes? :eyes:
Raj: saw this on the runtime dashboard 2m ago. p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~ 1.1s -> 3.8s for streaming endpoints (/v1/stream) for Cerulean tenant. lots of stalled streams with lots of open KV cache entries.
Sofia: adding context from model side — Cerulean has large multi-line prompts with repetitive prefixes, high concurrency (200-300 concurrent sessions) from a single IP pool. That interacts poorly with prefix-KV caching and continuous batching.
Liam (Cerulean): yep we pushed a campaign ~10:30 with many long templates. We can throttle on our side if needed. Are you seeing per-replica saturation?
Maya (oncall): checking replicas... API shows 8 replicas in the tenant pool, all at CPU 85-95% and one with GPU mem pressure. queue depth spiking. tagging eng-runtime @Raj
Raj: probable cause: prefix fanout + KV cache thrash. Long prefixes mean cache misses then huge KV writes. High concurrency causes batch sizes to drop and latency to pile. Recommend quick mitigations:
- temporarily route Cerulean to fallback model variant (smaller quantized) to reduce GPU mem and latency
- disable prefix KV caching for Cerulean tenant
- increase pool replicas by +3 (fast scale)
- request Cerulean to throttle campaign if possible
Maya (oncall): doing fast mitigations now. @ops-bot scale +3 replicas
ops-bot: Scaling command accepted: pool c-cerulean-prod replicas +3. Rolling start... ETA ~90s.
Maya (oncall): also toggling prefix caching off for tenant via runtime flag
Raj: command to disable prefix cache (internal):
```
redwoodctl tenant update c-cerulean-prod --set runtime.kv_cache.enabled=false
```
Maya (oncall): applied. hitting confirm on the flag toggle... done. monitoring.
Sofia: I'll prepare a canary fallback model route. Suggest routing 30% of requests to `cerulean-fallback:v1-quant` to reduce memory pressure and observe quality.
Ana: notify customer success and engineering engagement. Liam, can Cerulean absorb 30% fallback traffic? if quality dips we'll throttle back.
Liam (Cerulean): 30% is fine for now, please proceed. We'll pause the campaign if things don't improve in 10m. Thanks.
Maya (oncall): scale finished, replicas now 11. queue depth dropping slightly. p95 now 800ms, p99 2.4s — some improvement.
Raj: rolling the fallback route now. routing command:
```
redwoodctl routing set c-cerulean-prod --route /v1/stream cerulean-fallback:v1-quant=30% cerulean-prod:stable=70%
```
ops-bot: Routing update accepted.
Sofia: observing outputs — streaming chunks are arriving more regularly on fallback. quality check ready.
Maya (oncall): p95 down to 520ms, p99 1.4s. still some long tails but trending down. marking incident as "mitigating". paging severity -> sev2.
Raj: for long-term: need automatic detection for prefix-heavy tenants + adaptive cache TTL and per-tenant batching policy. I'll file an RFC after stabilization.
Ana: I'll loop in solutions and CS to coordinate follow-up and customer message. @Liam thanks for quick patch.
Liam (Cerulean): thanks team — we saw a few user errors during campaign but overall ok. we'll pause additional pushes until confirmed stable.
Maya (oncall): continuing to monitor for 30m. if p99 < 1s and stream stutter gone we'll close. leaving a note for postmortem draft: include root cause (prefix fanout x KV thrash), mitigations (scale, disable prefix cache, fallback routing), customer impact (stream stalls, elevated latency, degraded throughput), and next steps.
ops-bot: Incident timeline marker: mitigation applied at 3299991298 (scale), 3299991330 (kv cache disabled), 3299991365 (fallback route)
Sofia: will capture sample traces and prompt sets for eval so we can measure quality regression on fallback. attaching links in the postmortem.
Maya (oncall): thanks all — handoff to afternoon oncall @Raj in 25m unless someone wants to stay. I'll update the incident tracker and CS.
Raj: I'll stay and watch for 20m then draft the postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigating -> monitoring. severity: S2. participants: Maya, Raj, Sofia, Ana, Liam.
